When do Americans make calls and send messages?

On an average weekday, the share of Americans on calls, mail, or messages peaks at 9:00 PM, when 1.2% of people age 15 and older (about 3.1 million) are on calls, mail, or messages. On weekends it peaks at 8:00 PM (1.1%). Averaged over all days, Americans spend 7 min a day on calls, mail, or messages.

What it includes

Average time per weekday, for the activities in this group that take the most time.

  • Telephone calls to/from friends, neighbors, or acquaintances: 3 min a day
  • Telephone calls to/from family members: 2 min a day
  • Telephone calls, other: 2 min a day

About these numbers

Estimates come from all 258,954 diaries in the American Time Use Survey (Bureau of Labor Statistics and Census Bureau), 2003–2025, weighted to the U.S. civilian population age 15 and older and pooled across years. Times are local clock time. Counts are people on an average day of that type, not a live count. Weekdays are Monday–Friday. How the estimates work.
